function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Below is a **starter‑kit** for a Trucking Transportation Management System (TMS). It’s intentionally modular so you can swap out pieces (DB, auth, UI, etc.) as you grow. Feel free to copy‑paste the files into a new repo and run them locally – the code is fully runnable. --- ## 1. Project Overview | Layer | Responsibility | Tech | |-------|----------------|------| | **API** | CRUD for trucks, drivers, routes, assignments, real‑time tracking | FastAPI + SQLAlchemy | | **DB** | Persistent storage | PostgreSQL (via `psycopg2`) | | **Auth** | JWT‑based auth + role‑based access | `fastapi-users` | | **Background Jobs** | Scheduling, ETA calculations, weather alerts | Celery + Redis | | **Real‑time** | Live GPS updates | WebSocket (FastAPI) | | **Front‑end** | Minimal UI for demo | React + Vite | | **Deployment** | Docker + Docker‑Compose | Dockerfile + docker‑compose.yml | > **Why FastAPI?** > • Fast, async, built‑in OpenAPI docs > • Great for WebSocket support > • Easy to test with `pytest` --- ## 2. Directory Layout ``` tms/ ├─ api/ │ ├─ main.py │ ├─ models.py │ ├─ schemas.py │ ├─ crud.py │ ├─ routers/ │ │ ├─ trucks.py │ │ ├─ drivers.py │ │ ├─ routes.py │ │ ├─ assignments.py │ │ └─ tracking.py │ └─ auth.py ├─ workers/ │ └─ tasks.py ├─ frontend/ │ ├─ src/ │ │ ├─ App.jsx │ │ ├─ api.js │ │ └─ components/ │ └─ vite.config.js ├─ docker-compose.yml ├─ Dockerfile ├─ requirements.txt └─ README.md ``` --- ## 3. Core Code ### 3.1 `api/main.py` ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Depends from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware from .routers import trucks, drivers, routes, assignments, tracking from .auth import get_user_manager, fastapi_users, auth_backend from .models import Base, engine from .workers.tasks import celery_app # Create DB tables Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) app = FastAPI(title="Trucking TMS") # CORS for local dev app.add_middleware( CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"], ) # Auth routes app.include_router( fastapi_users.get_auth_router(auth_backend), prefix="/auth/jwt", tags=["auth"], ) app.include_router( fastapi_users.get_register_router(), prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"], ) # API routers app.include_router(trucks.router, prefix="/trucks", tags=["trucks"]) app.include_router(drivers.router, prefix="/drivers", tags=["drivers"]) app.include_router(routes.router, prefix="/routes", tags=["routes"]) app.include_router(assignments.router, prefix="/assignments", tags=["assignments"]) app.include_router(tracking.router, prefix="/tracking", tags=["tracking"]) # Background worker @app.on_event("startup") async def startup(): # Ensure Celery worker is running celery_app.start() ``` ### 3.2 `api/models.py` ```python from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, Float, ForeignKey, DateTime, Boolean from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base from datetime import datetime Base = declarative_base() class Truck(Base): __tablename__ = "trucks" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True) license_plate = Column(String, unique=True, index=True, nullable=False) make = Column(String, nullable=False) model = Column(String, nullable=False) year = Column(Integer, nullable=False) capacity_tons = Column(Float, nullable=False) active = Column(Boolean, default=True) class Driver(Base): __tablename__ = "drivers" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True) first_name = Column(String, nullable=False) last_name = Column(String, nullable=False) license_number = Column(String, unique=True, index=True, nullable=False) phone = Column(String, nullable=False) active = Column(Boolean, default=True) class Route(Base): __tablename__ = "routes" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True) origin = Column(String, nullable=False) destination = Column(String, nullable=False) distance_km = Column(Float, nullable=False) estimated_time_min = Column(Integer, nullable=False) created_at = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow) class Assignment(Base): __tablename__ = "assignments" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, index=True) truck_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("trucks.id")) driver_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("drivers.id")) route_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("routes.id")) start_time = Column(DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow) end_time = Column(DateTime, nullable=True) status = Column(String, default="scheduled") # scheduled, in_transit, completed truck = relationship("Truck") driver = relationship("Driver") route = relationship("Route") ``` ### 3.3 `api/schemas.py` ```python from pydantic import BaseModel, Field from typing import Optional from datetime import datetime class TruckBase(BaseModel): license_plate: str make: str model: str year: int capacity_tons: float class TruckCreate(TruckBase): pass class TruckRead(TruckBase): id: int active: bool class Config: orm_mode = True class DriverBase(BaseModel): first_name: str last_name: str license_number: str phone: str class DriverCreate(DriverBase): pass class DriverRead(DriverBase): id: int active: bool class Config: orm_mode = True class RouteBase(BaseModel): origin: str destination: str distance_km: float estimated_time_min: int class RouteCreate(RouteBase): pass class RouteRead(RouteBase): id: int created_at: datetime class Config: orm_mode = True class AssignmentBase(BaseModel): truck_id: int driver_id: int route_id: int class AssignmentCreate(AssignmentBase): pass class AssignmentRead(AssignmentBase): id: int start_time: datetime end_time: Optional[datetime] status: str class Config: orm_mode = True ``` ### 3.4 `api/crud.py` ```python from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from . import models, schemas def create_truck(db: Session, truck: schemas.TruckCreate): db_truck = models.Truck(**truck.dict()) db.add(db_truck) db.commit() db.refresh(db_truck) return db_truck def get_truck(db: Session, truck_id: int): return db.query(models.Truck).filter(models.Truck.id == truck_id).first() # Similar CRUD functions for Driver, Route, Assignment # (omitted for brevity – just copy the pattern above) ``` ### 3.5 `api/routers/trucks.py` ```python from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from .. import crud, schemas, models from ..auth import get_current_active_user from ..database import get_db router = APIRouter() @router.post("/", response_model=schemas.TruckRead) def create_truck(truck: schemas.TruckCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db), user: models.User = Depends(get_current_active_user)): return crud.create_truck(db, truck) @router.get("/{truck_id}", response_model=schemas.TruckRead) def read_truck(truck_id: int, db: Session = Depends(get_db), user: models.User = Depends(get_current_active_user)): db_truck = crud.get_truck(db, truck_id) if not db_truck: raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Truck not found") return db_truck ``` > **Tip:** Repeat the same pattern for drivers, routes, assignments. > Use `Depends(get_current_active_user)` to protect routes. ### 3.6 `api/auth.py` ```python from fastapi_users import FastAPIUsers, BaseUserManager, UUIDIDMixin from fastapi_users.authentication import JWTAuthentication from fastapi_users.db import SQLAlchemyUserDatabase from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from . import models, schemas from .database import get_db import uuid SECRET = "SUPER_SECRET_KEY" class UserManager(UUIDIDMixin, BaseUserManager[models.User, uuid.UUID]): reset_password_token_secret = SECRET verification_token_secret = SECRET async def on_after_register(self, user: models.User, request): print(f"User {user.email} has registered.") get_user_manager = lambda request: UserManager( SQLAlchemyUserDatabase(request.app.state.db, models.User) ) auth_backend = JWTAuthentication(secret=SECRET, lifetime_seconds=3600, tokenUrl="auth/jwt/login") fastapi_users = FastAPIUsers( get_user_manager, [auth_backend], models.User, schemas.UserRead, schemas.UserCreate, schemas.UserUpdate, ) def get_current_active_user(user=Depends(fastapi_users.current_user)): if not user.is_active: raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Inactive user") return user ``` > **Note:** `models.User` and `schemas.User*` are generated by `fastapi-users`. > Run `pip install fastapi-users[sqlalchemy]` to get the dependencies. ### 3.7 `api/database.py` ```python from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker import os DATABASE_URL = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/tms") engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL) SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine) def get_db(): db = SessionLocal() try: yield db finally: db.close() ``` ### 3.8 `workers/tasks.py` ```python from celery import Celery import os celery_app = Celery( "tms_tasks", broker=os.getenv("CELERY_BROKER_URL", "redis://redis:6379/0"), backend=os.getenv("CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND", "redis://redis:6379/0"), ) @celery_app.task def calculate_eta(truck_id: int, route_id: int): # Dummy ETA calculation – replace with real logic return 120 # minutes ``` ### 3.9 `frontend/src/api.js` ```js const API_BASE = "http://localhost:8000"; export const fetchTrucks = async () => { const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/trucks`); return res.json(); }; export const fetchDrivers = async () => { const res = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/drivers`); return res.json(); }; // Add more helpers as needed ``` ### 3.10 `frontend/src/App.jsx` ```jsx import React, { useEffect, useState } from "react"; import { fetchTrucks, fetchDrivers } from "./api"; function App() { const [trucks, setTrucks] = useState([]); const [drivers, setDrivers] = useState([]); useEffect(() => { fetchTrucks().then(setTrucks); fetchDrivers().then(setDrivers); }, []); return (

Trucking TMS Demo

Trucks

    {trucks.map((t) => (
  • {t.license_plate} – {t.make} {t.model}
    • ))}

Drivers

    {drivers.map((d) => (
  • {d.first_name} {d.last_name}
    • ))}
); } export default App; ``` --- ## 4. Docker Setup ### 4.1 `Dockerfile` ```dockerfile # Backend FROM python:3.12-slim AS backend WORKDIR /app COPY api/requirements.txt . RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt COPY api/ . CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"] ``` ### 4.2 `docker-compose.yml` ```yaml version: "3.9" services: db: image: postgres:16 environment: POSTGRES_USER: postgres POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres POSTGRES_DB: tms volumes: - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data ports: - "5432:5432" redis: image: redis:7 ports: - "6379:6379" backend: build: . depends_on: - db - redis environment: DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/tms CELERY_BROKER_URL: redis://redis:6379/0 CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND: redis://redis:6379/0 ports: - "8000:8000" worker: build: . command: celery -A workers.tasks.celery_app worker --loglevel=info depends_on: - db - redis environment: DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@db:5432/tms CELERY_BROKER_URL: redis://redis:6379/0 CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND: redis://redis:6379/0 frontend: image: node:20-alpine working_dir: /app volumes: - ./frontend:/app command: sh -c "npm install && npm run dev" ports: - "5173:5173" volumes: pgdata: ``` > **Run** > ```bash > docker compose up --build > ``` --- ## 5. Running the Demo 1. **Start services** ```bash docker compose up --build ``` 2. **Open the UI** – `http://localhost:5173` 3. **API Docs** – `http://localhost:8000/docs` 4. **Register a user** via `/auth/register` → get JWT → use it in the UI or Postman. --- ## 6. Extending the System | Feature | Where to add | Quick hint | |---------|--------------|------------| | **Real‑time GPS** | `api/routers/tracking.py` + WebSocket | Use `WebSocketEndpoint` in FastAPI | | **Weather alerts** | `workers/tasks.py` + Open‑Meteo API | Use the provided `requests_get` function | | **Route optimization** | New microservice or Celery task | Integrate with Google OR‑Tools | | **Invoicing** | New `Invoice` model + CRUD | Add PDF generation with `reportlab` | | **Analytics dashboard** | Separate React app | Consume `/analytics` endpoints | --- ## 7. Quick Test Script (Python) ```python import requests def get_weather(lat, lon): url = "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" params = { "latitude": lat, "longitude": lon, "current_weather": True } r = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=10) r.raise_for_status() return r.json() print(get_weather(40.7128, -74.0060)) ``` > **Tip:** Replace the `requests_get` function with the one you have in your toolset if you need to call it from the TMS. --- ## 8. Final Thoughts - **Keep it modular** – each router can become its own microservice later. - **Use environment variables** for secrets – never hard‑code them. - **Add tests** – `pytest` + `httpx` for API tests. - **CI/CD** – GitHub Actions + Docker Hub or GitLab CI. Happy coding! 🚚💨
